title: Reject broken links in the built documentation

build.command: pnpm registry:build && pnpm gallery:manifest && pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build

checker_on_real_dist.finding: The real (incomplete) build carries two genuinely broken canonical-origin links in the ledger bulk-add section: `https://rnraielements.com/r/nativewind` and `https://rnraielements.com/r/uniwind` (bare engine base URLs — the deployed site returns 404 for both). The checker names both with source `registry/index.html`; the 61-file/1171-link traversal still completes. Fixing the ledger page is ORI-AST-002/ORI-AST-007 scope, out of scope here; the checker's correct failure is the gate behaving as designed on an incomplete build.

red.observed: stub checker prints no traversal evidence — 'traversal counts emitted html files' fails (expected /\d+ html files/, received '').

green.observed: baseline fixture (real 61-page build + seeded /docs/introduction, /docs/owns-vs-does-not-own, /404, and the PRD redirects) exits 0; 67 html files / 1195 internal links; the /components/message link resolves identically in root-relative, relative (../../components/message), and canonical-origin (https://rnraielements.com/components/message) forms; /r/{nativewind,uniwind}/message.json resolve as files without index.html; the captured /_astro/ stylesheet resolves; the meta-refresh /docs redirect is recognized and its destination resolves.

red.observed: stub checker exits 0 after a target deletion — 'message-document deletion fails the gate: expected +0 not to be +0'.

green.observed: 5 independent owned-copy drills (delete message document, boundary document, /404 recovery target, redirect destination, /_astro asset) each exit nonzero naming source + URL; each restoration re-passes; empty and absent output both exit nonzero naming the path; baseline SHA-256 stable before/after.

red.observed: stub checker exits 0 after the row-message ID is removed — 'missing fragment fails the gate: expected +0 not to be +0'.

green.observed: plain (/registry#row-message), relative (../../registry#row-message), canonical (https://rnraielements.com/registry#row-message), encoded (/registry#row%2Dmessage), and same-document (#getting-started) fragments all resolve; removing only row-message's id attribute fails with `docs/introduction/index.html -> /registry#row-message: fragment #row-message not found in target document` (a fragment failure, not a missing-document); restoring the id re-passes.

red.observed: stub checker performs no HTTP — 'ordinary 404 produces a warning: expected '' to contain warning'.

green.observed: 6 real external requests are made; the 5 default required references return 200..299 and pass (exit 0); an ordinary 404 anchor warns (source + URL + HTTP 404, exit 0); the same URL declared via --required hard-fails (error, exit 1) while the default required set is preserved.

external_http_evidence.note: reachability only — a passing external check proves the URL is reachable, never that live useChat/provider/native behavior works (that verification belongs to the AI SDK and native tasks).

missing-document.sample: docs/introduction/index.html -> ../../components/message: no such target in the build

missing-fragment.sample: docs/introduction/index.html -> /registry#row-message: fragment #row-message not found in target document

redirect-destination.sample: r/nativewind/index.html -> /registry: no such target in the build

fixtures.description: owned scratch copies under node:os.tmpdir() seeded from the real `pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build` output; the not-yet-landed manuscript routes (/docs/introduction, /docs/owns-vs-does-not-own, /404) and the PRD redirects are added to owned copies only — never to shared source. The two bare engine-base-URL links in the real /registry page are repaired in the fixture via /r/{engine}/index.html meta-refresh redirects so the complete-build baseline can exit 0; this repair is documented and the underlying real break is reported by the checker on the unmodified real dist.
fixtures.scratch_roots: mkdtempSync(node:os.tmpdir()) — cleaned up after each drill and in afterAll
